notes: LIBRIVOX: The language filter id for Latin on librivox.org advanced search is recorded_language=39 (the search endpoint needs the header X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest; it returns JSON with an HTML 'results' field). All Latin-language projects were enumerated (4 pages). Complete solo/collaborative Latin projects: Caesar BG, Aeneid, Georgics, Eclogues, Augustine Confessions and De Civitate Dei, De Imitatione Christi, Boethius, Regula Benedicti, Seneca Epistulae selectae, Lucretius, Cato De Agricultura, Clarke's Aesop (1787), Historia Apollonii, Psalm 22, Horace Ars Poetica/Carmen Saeculare, Versio Latina Odyssey VI. Everything else Latin on LibriVox is single sections inside multilingual/carol/language-learning collections. No project page states the pronunciation used, so audio_pronunciation is 'desconhecida' throughout. LibriVox licence page: recordings are public domain 'definitely in the USA, and maybe in your country as well'; no attribution required but preferred. I set hosting_allowed=true for the LibriVox recordings of pre-1900 texts, but the editor should note LibriVox's own caveat about non-US jurisdictions and that the practical choice is to link to the archive.org mirrors (all verified HTTP 200), which also avoids hosting 100 MB-1.6 GB zips. Source-text scans linked from the project pages were HEAD-checked (HTTP 200) and their Internet Archive metadata read for edition details. HACKETT: product pages live under https://hackettpublishing.com/lingua-latina-per-se-illustrata-series/... (the /search?q= endpoint is 404; use /catalogsearch/result/?q=). The official site offers NO free audio samples; audio is sold as 'Familia Romana Latine Audio Files' (classical or ecclesiastical pronunciation) and streamed inside the paid Familia Romana Essentials Online course (US$39.95/12 months). The only free item is a zip of 'Transparency Masters' images for qualified adopters on request. The CD-ROM of images is discontinued. Textbook content was not quoted. TOOLS: latin-words.com has no licence text on the page; the licence quoted comes from Whitaker's own statement in the mk270/whitakers-words README (fetched). archives.nd.edu/words.html still returns 200 but is a stub. Logeion's main page is a JS app with no text for crawlers; licence info taken from its about-logeion-ios.html page. Perseus was down (503) during this session. The Latin Library has no licence; About page fetched and quoted. Vicipaedia is CC BY-SA 4.0. PORTUGUESE: the only open-licensed, university-published Portuguese Latin course found is Leni Ribeiro Leite's 'Latine loqui' (EDUFES 2021, 2 vols, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 per the UFES DSpace metadata; PDFs served by the DSpace REST 'content' endpoints as application/pdf). Being NC-ND it is link-only. The Brazilian commercial grammars (Napoleão Mendes de Almeida; Rezende's Latina Essentia) were not reported because no official publisher page was found. A 2024 UFES doctoral thesis on extensive reading in Brazilian Latin teaching (handle 10/20789, CC BY-ND) turned up in the same repository search and may interest the editor for pedagogy, but it is not a learner resource.
